concepts.name: Purpose of user research
concepts.summary: Explain that user research uncovers real behaviors, needs and context so teams decide on evidence rather than assumptions.

concepts.name: Behavior versus opinion
concepts.summary: Distinguish what people do from what they say they do or would do, and why observed behavior is stronger evidence.

concepts.name: Qualitative versus quantitative data
concepts.summary: Describe how qualitative methods explain why and quantitative methods measure how many or how much.

concepts.name: Research participants and users
concepts.summary: Recall that participants should resemble the people who will actually use the product, not colleagues or friends.

concepts.name: Common research method types
concepts.summary: Name the main methods such as interviews, usability tests, surveys, diary studies and card sorting and what each is for.

concepts.name: Research questions and goals
concepts.summary: Explain that a study starts from a clear question about what the team needs to learn.

concepts.name: Informed consent and privacy
concepts.summary: Recall that participants must understand the study, agree voluntarily and have their data protected.

misconceptions.text: Asking users what they want is enough to know what to build.
Five friends or coworkers are as good as real target users for research.
Qualitative research is unreliable because it is not numbers.

concepts.name: Writing neutral interview questions
concepts.summary: Write open, non-leading questions about past behavior instead of hypotheticals or yes/no prompts.

concepts.name: Discussion guide structure
concepts.summary: Build a guide with introduction, warm-up, core topics, probes and wrap-up that fits the session time.

concepts.name: Screeners and recruiting criteria
concepts.summary: Turn target-user traits into screener questions that qualify participants without revealing the right answers.

concepts.name: Usability task scenarios
concepts.summary: Write realistic goal-based tasks that avoid naming interface labels or hinting at the path.

concepts.name: Moderated usability test session
concepts.summary: Run a task-based session using think-aloud, neutral prompts and observation without helping or defending the design.

concepts.name: Note-taking and observation capture
concepts.summary: Record observations, quotes and timestamps separately from interpretations during sessions.

concepts.name: Sample size for qualitative studies
concepts.summary: Understand why small iterative rounds of about five per segment reveal most major usability problems.

misconceptions.text: Good interview questions ask people whether they would use a feature.
A moderator should help participants when they get stuck so the session continues smoothly.
Screeners should state the desired profile so participants can self-identify.

concepts.name: Method selection by question
concepts.summary: Analyse a research question and constraints to pick a method that fits, such as attitudinal versus behavioral and generative versus evaluative.

concepts.name: Contextual inquiry
concepts.summary: Observe and interview people in their own environment while they do real work, using the master-apprentice approach.

concepts.name: Diary studies
concepts.summary: Design prompts, duration and reminders so participants log experiences over time with manageable effort.

concepts.name: Survey design and bias
concepts.summary: Design surveys with clear scales, balanced options and ordering, and identify sampling and response bias.

concepts.name: Unmoderated remote testing
concepts.summary: Set up self-guided tasks with clear instructions and success measures, and judge their tradeoffs against moderated sessions.

concepts.name: Card sorting and tree testing
concepts.summary: Run open and closed card sorts and tree tests to learn users' mental models of categories and findability.

concepts.name: Affinity mapping synthesis
concepts.summary: Cluster observations bottom-up into themes and separate evidence from interpretation to produce insights.

concepts.name: Severity rating of findings
concepts.summary: Rate issues by frequency, impact and persistence to prioritise what the team should fix.

misconceptions.text: Surveys can explain why users behave as they do.
Affinity mapping means grouping notes by predefined categories.
Unmoderated tests are simply a cheaper replacement for moderated tests.

concepts.name: Evidence-based personas
concepts.summary: Build and critique personas grounded in observed behavior patterns and quotes rather than demographics or stereotypes.

concepts.name: Journey mapping from observed data
concepts.summary: Construct journey maps showing stages, actions, thoughts, emotions and pain points traced back to research evidence.

concepts.name: Triangulating multiple methods
concepts.summary: Combine qualitative and quantitative sources, judging where they agree or conflict, to strengthen conclusions.

concepts.name: Recruiting hard-to-reach segments
concepts.summary: Plan sourcing, incentives and screening for specialist or vulnerable groups while managing sampling bias.

concepts.name: Interview and moderation bias analysis
concepts.summary: Analyse recordings for leading, confirmation and social desirability effects and correct the approach.

concepts.name: Insight framing and recommendations
concepts.summary: Turn findings into evidence-backed insights and recommendations tailored to stakeholder decisions.

concepts.name: Research ethics and data governance
concepts.summary: Evaluate consent, anonymisation, retention and vulnerable-participant risks in a study design.

misconceptions.text: A persona needs a name, photo and demographics to be useful.
When survey data and interview findings disagree, one of them must be wrong.
A journey map is a workshop artifact that can be drawn from team assumptions.

concepts.name: Evaluating evidence quality
concepts.summary: Judge the validity, reliability and limits of studies, including those run by others, and decide how much weight to give them.

concepts.name: Research program strategy
concepts.summary: Design a portfolio of studies aligned to product strategy, balancing generative and evaluative work over time.

concepts.name: Research democratisation governance
concepts.summary: Create guidelines, training and review so non-researchers can run research without eroding quality or ethics.

concepts.name: Research repository and insight systems
concepts.summary: Design tagging and storage that make findings traceable, reusable and findable across projects.

concepts.name: Adapting methods to constraints
concepts.summary: Invent or tailor methods for tight timelines, remote contexts or novel products while defending the tradeoffs.

concepts.name: Influencing decisions with research
concepts.summary: Evaluate how findings affect decisions and shape communication and stakeholder involvement to increase impact.

concepts.name: Cross-cultural and inclusive research
concepts.summary: Assess and adapt study design for cultural, accessibility and language differences so findings generalise appropriately.

misconceptions.text: Scaling research means letting anyone run studies with a template.
Strong findings automatically lead to action by stakeholders.
A rigorous method is one fixed protocol applied identically everywhere.
